title: Kennedy Active-Countdown Prescribed Burn Operation
summary: NASA records a January 2026 operational adaptation in which Kennedy and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service conducted two prescribed burns totaling about 2,600 acres during an active launch countdown.
key_findings: NASA describes the event as the first active-countdown prescribed burn at Kennedy.
The operation coordinated spaceport, wildlife-service, commercial-partner, weather, personnel, road, and launch considerations.
NASA links the adaptation to a corridor that exceeded 100 successful liftoffs in 2025.
why_it_matters: It supplies an operating record for managing ecological resilience alongside higher launch cadence.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a real multi-agency spaceport operation rather than another plan.
Connects climate, habitat, safety, access, and launch operations.
Creates later checks for repeatability and measured resilience outcomes.
evidence_limits: One operation does not establish a sustained capability or trend.
The record does not quantify launch-delay, safety, wildfire, or ecological outcomes.
